body: further test, rclone 1.56.0 starts to encode authorize command, and token returns from local machine becomes longer than previous versions. 1.55.0 1.55.1 all working ok, standard "authorize client_ID client_secret " and returns shorter token
@animosity22  I guess you meant to add the OneDrive label instead of OpenDrive label

I guess the easiest solution to this is to increase the buffer size...

Can you give this a go?

[v1.58.0-beta.5907.1d53714ab.fix-5835-config](https://beta.rclone.org/branch/fix-5835-config/v1.58.0-beta.5907.1d53714ab.fix-5835-config/) on branch [fix-5835-config](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/fix-5835-config) (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

just tried 1.58 build. the token input field still doesn't accept token longer than 4096

to simply reproduce issue, you can:

add a profile with onedrive backend,

type anything for client id and secrect
choose N headless machine
copy and paste any random string longer than 4096 (eg 5000 chars) into the token field and copy and paste the pasted token from the field back to editor to measure the length (eg. notepad++ to check the length.) you will find the successfully pasted token into that token field is 4095~4096, the filed will not accept anything long than that. 

all rclone versions don't accept token longer than 4096. The issue is the rclone that is generateing the token used to be non-encoded and always smaller than 4096. after version 1.56, authorize code starts to get encoded thus the return token is encoded too which makes it longer than 4096 to not be able to fit into the token field.

I think this must be a Windows or maybe ssh limitation - it works fine for me on Linux locally.

You should be able to get going using the [copying the config file](https://rclone.org/remote_setup/#configuring-by-copying-the-config-file) technique.

However this is a problem we need to fix...

body:
See also https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/5630, https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/2732

We've had enough versions of this issue...

I guess tokens are only ever going to get bigger, unlike keyboard paste buffers!

This needs a better fix...

Maybe we should, if we get a decode error, show the user the last 100 characters of the paste and ask if they would like to add more data onto the paste? That would at least let the user fix the problem with another paste of the remaining bits?
